notes_extra: 7.5 twist. Best seated very close to the lands or 0.100 off. COAL: 2.90 or 2.80 for his reamer.

notes_extra: 140 hybrids and H4350 in all three of their 6.5CM rifles. He also wrote 6.5 Creed in the same post.

author: boltman13
notes_extra: Jumping 0.010 in. The same post's 41.4 gr H4350 load is the 144 gr Long Range Hybrid, not this bullet.

author: Roperboy87
notes_extra: Jumping .30 thousand.

author: cfreeman
notes_extra: Thread is part 26414, Fed SR Match primers, and H4350. His rifle is a Krieger. A buddy with a Shilen and CCI 450s ended at 43 gr. He also named nodes around 41.5 and 42.5-43.

author: Lefty Trigger
notes_extra: Thread is part 26414.

author: rsbhunter
notes_extra: One of two Savage factory 6.5 creeds. He said he could go higher. Thread is part 26414.

author: rsbhunter
notes_extra: The other Savage factory 6.5 creed. Thread is part 26414.

author: PatMiles
notes_extra: 26 in PVA barrel on an RPR. Jumping .040 in with .002 in neck tension.

author: David Christian
notes_extra: B140H in two different length 6.5CM barrels. Jump about .015 to .025 in. He would not chase the higher node around 42 gr.

author: garandman
notes_extra: He called 41.5 gr over the listed max charge, with only minimal pressure signs and slightly flattened primers.

author: Firestone
notes_extra: Thread is Berger Hybrid Target 140 gr and H4350 for NRL Hunter.

author: wind gypsy
notes_extra: Factory Tikka 24.3 in CTR. Twice-fired Lapua LRP. Seated somewhere over 2.9 in. Suppressor on, temperatures in the 50s. Average of 10 or more shots.

author: wind gypsy
notes_extra: Same Tikka 24.3 in CTR and Lapua LRP. He swapped the suppressor and the temperature was about 20 degrees cooler than the 42.0 gr string. Average of 10 or more shots.

author: Wyoming Shooter
notes_extra: Tikka T3X CTR 20 in barrel. The same charge with a Hornady 140 ELD-M was 2617 fps.

author: Eric Leonard
notes_extra: Worked up from 34 gr by 0.4 gr. 37.4 gr started touching and 38.6 gr went through the same hole at 100 yards. A little pressure on the primers, no sticky bolt. He stopped at 38.6 gr. Jump .015 in. No velocity yet.

author: Eric Leonard
notes_extra: He wrote 140 Hybird. Shot well at 800 yards. A shiny spot on the case showed at 38.8 gr and he did not go higher.

author: Eric Leonard
notes_extra: He stopped at 41.5 gr without a chronograph. .288 in nitride bushing, no-turn neck. The same post's estimated just-touching COAL of 2.857 in is a measurement, not this charge's seating.

author: ChrisA
notes_extra: He called 40.2 gr max for him.

author: jpmimproved
notes_extra: Seated .030 in off the lands.

author: JLT
notes_extra: He called the pressure modest. No velocity number in that post. His separate 54.0 gr note of about 3,050 fps was for a 140 gr bullet he did not name as the Hybrid.

author: vervi1jw
notes_extra: Match load. He also used H4831sc and said he had run the hybrids into the 2900s without a charge for that speed.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Seekins Havak 2, new Lapua, 24 in. Started 0.040 in off the lands. Pressure-test step.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Seekins Havak 2 pressure-test step.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Seekins Havak 2. He said the 58.5-59.0 gr window grouped tightly but was closer to pressure than he wanted in a new rifle.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Seekins Havak 2 pressure-test step. Same 58.5-59.0 gr window note.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Increased bolt lift and the start of marks on the brass.

author: cb4128
notes_extra: Same Seekins Havak 2 H1000 work. Seated .027 in off the lands. Bolt lift and brass looked good. No velocity in that post. Berger had told him 58.3 gr was max in a 26 in barrel with the same brass and bullet.

author: Masterdunbar
notes_extra: He later said the barrel had a +P throat, so the pressure is not the same as a SAAMI chamber.
